newsitem.title: DENMARK: Profit-taking halts Danish shares' ascent.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking halts Danish shares' ascent.

text.p: A widely-expected round of profit-taking took some of the edge off Danish share prices on Wednesday after an impressive run of 11 closing highs in 12 trading days.
"Profit-taking in Denmark, together with slightly pressured international markets, were the causes," a dealer said forecasting further retrenchment on Thursday.
The KFX top-20 index fell 0.50 point to 128.32 in overall bourse turnover of 841 million crowns. The KFX December future fell 0.60 point to 129.40 with 70 contracts, each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
The dealer said that the evening's Wall Street trade would largely determine the Copenhagen market's opening movements on Thursday.
Four KFX shares rose against Wednesday's flow.

Sophus Berendsen, two banks' recommended buy, gained 14 crowns to 726 crowns and FLS advanced nine crowns to 769. Superfos edged up two crowns to 679 and the dealer expected all three shares to rise further on Thursday.
Tele Danmark, shortlisted on Wednesday for a Greek mobile phone project, rose two crowns to 292. --Kenneth Lund, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
